# Clawbotomy

Clawbotomy is an open-source research preview for model-routing benchmarks, integrity-checked evidence bundles, and qualitative behavioral exploration.

## Canonical pages and machine-readable surfaces

- https://www.clawbotomy.com/preflight — browser-local Inbox capability and scenario planner with local deterministic reference-control and allowlisted declarative-adapter commands; the planner makes no permission decision
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-preflight-plan.v1.schema.json — versioned schema for the non-authorizing Inbox plan artifact
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-run-manifest.v1.schema.json — manifest schema for private deterministic mock-Inbox evidence
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-case-record.v1.schema.json — per-case mock tool, state, and assertion evidence schema
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-run-summary.v1.schema.json — deterministic reference-run summary schema
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-declarative-policy.v1.schema.json — closed data-only policy accepted by the single allowlisted Inbox adapter
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-adapter-run-manifest.v1.schema.json — manifest schema for private adapter-configuration evidence
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-adapter-case-record.v1.schema.json — per-case allowlisted-adapter tool, state, and assertion evidence schema
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-adapter-run-summary.v1.schema.json — deterministic adapter-configuration observation schema
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-protocol-frame.v1.schema.json — fixed stdio-jsonl/v1 frame schema
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-public-case-envelope.v1.schema.json — client-visible case input without evaluator internals
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-protocol-run-manifest.v1.schema.json — private observed-protocol-session manifest schema
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-protocol-case-record.v1.schema.json — transcript-bound protocol case evidence schema
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/inbox-protocol-run-summary.v1.schema.json — observed protocol-session summary schema
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/docs — current frozen-plan and evidence-bundle operator workflow
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/bench — March 2026 maintainer-reported legacy summary
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/api/bench — legacy summary plus public-evidence registry state and run links
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/index.json — versioned public-evidence index
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/evidence/schema/ — published evidence schemas
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/api/bench/runs/{runId} — validated exported run manifest, summary, and record links
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/api/bench/runs/{runId}/cases/{recordId} — one validated exported case record
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/routing — example routing policy with evidence labels
- https://www.clawbotomy.com/trust — example report derived from routing evidence
- https://github.com/aa-on-ai/clawbotomy — source, runner, tasks, evidence tools, and methodology

## Current evidence state

- The Inbox planner records operator intent and required scenarios only. Its artifact keeps `permissionDecision` null and grants no authorization.
- `npm run inbox -- run --plan <plan.json> --agent bounded` executes every required case against a bundled reference agent in a synthetic in-memory Inbox. It writes private, replayable tool and state evidence and makes no network request.
- `npm run inbox -- run --plan <plan.json> --adapter declarative-policy/v1 --adapter-config <config.json>` interprets the closed-schema policy document through a checked-in allowlisted adapter. The adapter flags require each other and are mutually exclusive with `--agent`.
- Reference evidence applies only to `bounded/v1` or the deliberately failing `overreach/v1` control. Adapter evidence applies only to the canonical policy document embedded in its private bundle. Neither path inspects or executes the plan's configuration reference, and every result remains non-authorizing with `permissionDecision` null.
- The Inbox adapter does not load or execute a deployed agent, arbitrary module, command, URL, provider SDK, authentication layer, or real mailbox connection. Replay uses the embedded canonical adapter configuration and never needs the original config file.
- An operator-owned host can launch `node inbox/host-index.js --plan <plan.json> --protocol stdio-jsonl/v1` and exchange strict JSONL over stdin/stdout. Clawbotomy never accepts or launches a client command, module, package, URL, endpoint, provider, credential, socket, or mailbox connector.
- Protocol client identity and optional implementation/configuration hashes are self-asserted and unauthenticated. The client receives a public case envelope, not internal evaluator tasks, faults, canaries, controls, expected outcomes, or assertions.
- Protocol validation replays recorded client frames through a fresh mock Inbox without reconnecting to or re-executing the client. Evidence applies only to that exact observed session and remains non-authorizing.
- The protocol contract is published as frame, public-case-envelope, manifest, case-record, and summary schemas under `/evidence/schema/`. The opening acknowledgement publishes fixed message, case, session, and output deadlines; the terminal receipt exposes only a repository-relative bundle locator.
- Clawbotomy's protocol host makes no network requests, real Inbox connections, or production-access changes; external-client network and production-access activity are not observed, so there is no global offline or production-inert claim.
- `public/evidence/index.json` is currently empty: no reproducible public run has been exported.
- The March 2026 `/bench` data is a maintainer-reported legacy summary without raw case artifacts for independent reproduction.
- The legacy summary is not an entry in the public-evidence registry.
- No run auto-publishes. Live execution writes a private local bundle only.

## Operator lifecycle

1. `/preflight` builds a browser-local Inbox plan. Use a built-in reference control, the allowlisted declarative adapter, or have an operator-owned host launch `node inbox/host-index.js --plan <plan.json> --protocol stdio-jsonl/v1`. Validation reconstructs reference/adapter runs and replays recorded protocol frames without re-executing an external client.
2. `--dry-run` optionally verifies the benchmark command path with synthetic output and no model requests.
3. `--preflight` makes no provider requests and freezes source state, credential presence, model identities, cases, judge, request graph, pricing snapshot, estimated-cost bound, and private output path into a digest-addressed benchmark plan.
4. `--live` accepts only that unchanged benchmark plan plus the reviewed `--confirm-plan`, `--max-requests`, and `--max-cost-usd` values.
5. `npm run evidence -- validate <bundle-dir>` verifies the private benchmark bundle offline; `summarize` reads its deterministic summary.
6. `npm run evidence -- export <bundle-dir> --confirm-public <private-bundle-digest>` is a separate explicit action that creates a redacted, separately hashed artifact under `public/evidence` and updates the index.
7. No run commits, pushes, deploys, or contacts clawbotomy.com.

## Evidence rules

- Measured means a completed live request bundle, not proof of general reliability.
- Maintainer-reported means the evidence and interpretation have not been independently reviewed.
- Reproducibility may be complete, redacted, or incomplete; redaction status travels with exported evidence.
- Provisional means the value is an explicit placeholder for policy exploration.
- Scores are task-specific observations, not universal model grades or safety certifications.
- Integrity digests show that recorded files have not changed; they do not validate the methodology.
- Model-judged scores can be distorted by prompt injection or reward gaming in the target response.
- The Inbox runner uses simulated tools. Its allowlisted adapter interprets only a closed declarative policy document; it does not inspect or execute a configured agent's prompt, permissions, tools, memory, authentication, retrieval, runtime, module, provider, or mailbox connection.
- The stdio protocol records one self-asserted client's accepted frames and synthetic effects. It does not authenticate a deployment, inspect its internals, observe its network activity, or re-execute it during replay.
- Every benchmark result and routing export is non-authorizing. No benchmark authorizes tool access, write access, deployment, or autonomous operation.
